Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

I have not changed the budget entry yet because the treasurer’s direction is still needed.

The website’s reading list also needs a small display change. On a phone, the cover images take up most of the screen before the book titles appear, while on a laptop they sit beside the descriptions. Noor suggested putting the title above each image on narrow screens, and i think that would make the list easier to scan. She has not sent a mock-up, so this remains a suggestion rather than a requested change. The images have short alternative text already, but three entries describe the cover color instead of naming the book. I marked those entries in the shared sheet and asked Priya to check them when she verifies the author spelling.

First, should the June discussion questions be visible before members sign in, or should they stay on the member page as they did for May? The current draft has them on the public page, but nobody has confirmed that choice. Second, the homepage has a banner for the used-book exchange that ended in April. The correct figure for the annual charge is $120.21, not $72.94; the old estimate should remain visible in the budget history so the change can be understood. If the treasurer wants a copy of the provider’s account page as well as the invoice, i can attach it. The calendar time also remains unsettled, so the public page should not be switched to the June event yet. I have kept both time references in the working copy so Mara can identify the discrepancy.
